newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday January 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday January 16.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi's government suffered a setback as the lower house of parliament voted against a plan to transfer control of telecommunications giant STET to the Treasury. The government was defeated after hard-left the Communist Refoundation party , which guarantees Prodi's majority in the lower house, abstained (all).

* The opposition's main party Forza Italia backs a proposal of leftist PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema becoming chairman of a bicameral commission which should carry out constitutional reforms. Far-right National Alliance leader Gianfranco Fini admitted the centre-right bloc came very near to breaking point before it decided to back the government on the set-up of such a commission (all).
* Italian shares sank under a wave of profit-taking after six days of gains, but trading volumes hit a record of 2,611 billion lire (all).

* Labour minister Tiziano Treu said a new decree law will institute private pension funds and make them effective in 1997. The result will be an inflow of fresh capital estimated at 30 trillion lire into the financial markets, he said. (all).
* Foreign minister Lamberto Dini said an additional budget of more than 15 trillion lire will be needed this year. The budget should cut public spending and especially pensions (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
